concepts.text: 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976) added three words: Socialist, Secular and Integrity
Full text of the Preamble
Source of authority: derives from the people of India
Nature of Indian State: Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic
Objectives of the Constitution: Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity
Date of adoption: November 26, 1949
Sovereign: meaning and implications
children: India is not a dependency or dominion of any other nation
India is an independent state with no authority above it
India is free to conduct its own affairs (both internal and external)
Full membership of the Commonwealth of Nations does not affect India's sovereignty
Acceptance of British Crown as head of the Commonwealth is an extra-constitutional declaration that does not affect sovereignty
Membership of the United Nations Organisation (UNO) does not limit sovereignty
India can acquire a foreign territory or cede a part of its territory
Historical background: dependency until Indian Independence Act 1947, dominion until January 26, 1950
Nehru's 1949 statement: Commonwealth is a free association by free will, alliance does not mean loss of independence, member-nation can freely leave

concepts.text: Socialist: meaning and features
children: Term added by 42nd Amendment (1976)
Socialist content was already implicit in Directive Principles of State Policy before the amendment
Congress party's Avadi session (1955) resolution to establish a 'socialistic pattern of society'
Indian brand is democratic socialism (mixed economy with co-existence of public and private sectors)
Contrasted with communistic socialism (state socialism) which involves nationalisation and abolition of private property
Supreme Court: democratic socialism aims to end poverty, ignorance, disease and inequality of opportunity
Indian socialism is a blend of Marxism and Gandhism, leaning heavily towards Gandhian socialism
New Economic Policy (1991) of liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation diluted socialist credentials
Indira Gandhi: own brand of socialism, not mere nationalisation

concepts.text: Secular: meaning and features
children: Term added by 42nd Amendment (1976)
Supreme Court (1974): Constitution-makers intended to establish a secular state even though not expressly mentioned
Articles 25 to 28 guarantee the fundamental right to freedom of religion
Indian Constitution embodies the positive concept of secularism (all religions have same status and support from state)
Three types of states based on attitude towards religion: atheistic (anti-religion), theocratic (state religion), secular (neutral)
Examples of secular states: USA and India
Definition of secularism by H.R. Gokhale (then Union Law Minister)
Definition of secularism by P.B. Gajendragadkar (former Chief Justice of India)

concepts.text: Democratic: meaning and features
children: Based on the doctrine of popular sovereignty
Types: direct democracy (people exercise supreme power directly, e.g., Switzerland) and indirect (representative democracy)
Devices of direct democracy: Referendum, Initiative, Recall, Plebiscite
India follows representative parliamentary democracy (executive responsible to legislature)
Manifestations: universal adult franchise, periodic elections, rule of law, independence of judiciary, absence of discrimination
'Democratic' used in broader sense embracing political, social and economic democracy
Dr. Ambedkar's concluding speech (Nov 25, 1949): political democracy cannot last without social democracy; liberty, equality and fraternity form a trinity
Without equality, liberty would produce supremacy of the few over the many; without liberty, equality would kill individual initiative
Supreme Court (1997): Constitution envisions to establish an egalitarian social order rendering social, economic and political justice

concepts.text: Republic: meaning and features
children: Head of state is elected (President)
President elected indirectly for a fixed period of five years
Political sovereignty vested in the people, not in a single individual like a king
No privileged class; all public offices open to every citizen without discrimination
Contrasted with monarchy (hereditary head of state, e.g., Britain)

concepts.text: Justice: meaning and forms
children: Embraces three distinct forms: social, economic and political
Secured through Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy
Social justice: equal treatment without distinctions of caste, colour, race, religion, sex; absence of privileges; improvement of backward classes (SCs, STs, OBCs) and women
Economic justice: non-discrimination based on economic factors; elimination of glaring inequalities in wealth, income and property
Combination of social and economic justice denotes 'distributive justice'
Political justice: equal political rights, equal access to political offices, equal voice in government
Ideal of justice taken from the Russian Revolution (1917)

concepts.text: Liberty: meaning and features
children: Absence of restraints on activities of individuals; providing opportunities for development of individual personalities
Preamble secures liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship through Fundamental Rights
Liberty is enforceable in a court of law in case of violation
Liberty is essential for the successful functioning of the Indian democratic system
Liberty does not mean 'license' to do what one likes; enjoyed within limitations mentioned in the Constitution
Liberty as conceived by the Preamble and Fundamental Rights is qualified, not absolute

concepts.text: Equality: meaning and three dimensions
children: Absence of special privileges to any section of society; provision of adequate opportunities for all without discrimination
Preamble secures equality of status and opportunity

Civic equality: equality before law (Article 14), prohibition of discrimination (Article 15), equality of opportunity in public employment (Article 16), abolition of untouchability (Article 17), abolition of titles (Article 18)

Political equality: no person ineligible for electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex (Article 325); elections to Lok Sabha and state assemblies on basis of adult suffrage (Article 326)
Economic equality: Directive Principles (Article 39) - equal right to adequate means of livelihood, equal pay for equal work

concepts.text: Fraternity: meaning and features
children: Sense of brotherhood
Constitution promotes fraternity through system of single citizenship

Fundamental Duties (Article 51-A): duty to promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood transcending religious, linguistic, regional or sectional diversities; duty to protect dignity of women; duty to uphold sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
Fraternity assures dignity of the individual and unity and integrity of the nation
'Integrity' added by 42nd Amendment (1976)
K.M. Munshi on dignity of individual: Constitution ensures material betterment and democratic set-up, recognises personality as sacred
Unity and integrity embraces psychological and territorial dimensions of national integration
India as a Union of States (Article 1) - states have no right to secede; indestructible nature of the Indian Union
Hindrances to national integration: communalism, regionalism, casteism, linguism, secessionism

concepts.text: K.M. Munshi: Preamble is the horoscope of our sovereign democratic republic
Sir Alladi Krishnaswami Iyer: Preamble expresses what we had thought or dreamt so long
Pandit Thakur Das Bhargava's descriptions of the Preamble

Preamble is a proper yardstick to measure the worth of the Constitution

concepts.text: Sir Ernest Barker: Preamble is the key-note to the Constitution; proud that India subscribes to a political tradition
M. Hidayatullah's statements on the Preamble
children: Preamble resembles the Declaration of Independence of the United States of America
Preamble is more than a declaration; it is the soul of the Constitution
Preamble lays down the pattern of political society
Preamble contains a solemn resolve which nothing but a revolution can alter

concepts.text: Berubari Union case (1960)
children: Arose from a reference by the President under Article 143 regarding implementation of Indo-Pakistan agreement
Supreme Court held Preamble shows general purposes behind provisions and can be used to resolve ambiguity
Supreme Court opined that Preamble is not a part of the Constitution

concepts.text: Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)
children: Supreme Court rejected the earlier opinion of Berubari Union
Held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution
Constitution should be read in light of the grand vision expressed in the Preamble
Edifice of Constitution is based on basic elements in Preamble; amending power cannot take away fundamental characteristics
Preamble is amendable under Article 368 but basic features cannot be altered

concepts.text: LIC of India case (1995)
Preamble was enacted after the rest of the Constitution to ensure conformity with the adopted Constitution
President of the Constituent Assembly's motion: 'The question is that Preamble stands part of the Constitution' – motion adopted
Preamble is non-justiciable (not enforceable in courts of law)
Preamble is neither a source of power to legislature nor a prohibition upon the powers of legislature
Amendability of the Preamble under Article 368
children: Preamble can be amended, subject to the condition that no amendment is done to the 'basic features'
Preamble has been amended only once so far (42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976)
The 42nd Amendment adding Socialist, Secular and Integrity was held valid
